evidence: a-dynamic-module-is-loaded-once-and-nginx-runs: baseline line 86 (nginx_cfg_prepend include '/etc/nginx/modules-enabled/*') declares that nginx.conf includes the enabled dynamic modules. Upstream's original module (puppet-nginx 0.13.0, line 42) had no include of its own, so the baseline produced exactly one include. The probe enables one module (libnginx-mod-stream) so that the include matters. The effect counts the enabled module file, then counts the include lines in nginx.conf (expects 1), then checks that nginx -t passes and that the service is active. mutates declares the action's whole change (package install + nginx restart). The action's own output goes to /dev/null, so the evidence is its result on disk and in the service. The action is a test stimulus for the include, not a command the line runs. That fits the header's batch-8 ruling-1 rationale.
dh-group-2048-bits-not-world-readable (line 36): $dh_params_bits = 2048 is the default under the defaults fixture. openssl dhparam -text reporting '(2048 bit)' tests exactly that value.

dh-group-2048-bits-not-world-readable (lines 140-143): the exec writes $base_dh_params=/etc/nginx/dhparams.pem with 'openssl dhparam -out ... 2048 && chmod u=rw,g=r,o=' (creates guard on the same path). stat '%a' == 640 is u=rw,g=r,o=, and the bit count is checked on that same file.
